clue.text: Coach wants good fighter on film

parts.note: Sven-Goran Eriksson was England's football coach, so a coach can be SVEN
Muhammad Ali, the boxer, is the classic crossword fighter

explanation.surface: A sports coach is after a combative player to appear in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'film': Svengali (1931) is about a hypnotist. Sven-Goran Eriksson coached the England football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the title of a 1931 movie about a sinister hypnotist.

clue.text: Pop, as do bubbles?

indicators.note: bubbles suggests letters fizzing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink, as the bubbles do, goes pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbles' rearranges 'as do'; pop is fizzy drink, and bubbles also describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy drink, a sweet carbonated beverage.

clue.text: They were lovers, finally gave it up

definitions.text: They were lovers, finally gave it up

parts.words: They were lovers, finally gave it up
parts.note: former partners who were once a couple but ended the relationship

explanation.surface: A couple who were once in love finally called it a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Former partners are people who once were a couple and split up.

clue.text: Sign up, say, and ultimately fit in very well

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the outer word

parts.note: sure! means very well, as a reply

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sign up and you will eventually fit in very nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the abbreviation for 'say' upwards to GE; 'in' puts T, the last letter of 'fit', inside the word for 'very well'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement made to signal something.

clue.text: Girl on set with H Ford -new film

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An actress on set alongside Harrison Ford for a new movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GIRLONSET plus HFORD. 'H Ford' evokes Harrison Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord of the Rings is Peter Jackson's fantasy movie trilogy.

clue.text: Was shown a remarkable short film

parts.note: a programme that ran was shown on screen

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: as in 'that's some car', SOME means a remarkable one

explanation.surface: Someone saw an impressive short movie screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from SOME, leaving SOM. Ran (1985) is Kurosawa's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran is the title of Akira Kurosawa's 1985 epic movie.

clue.text: Nasty crash overshadowing royal family of 17 4

indicators.note: overshadowing means the outer letters loom over and around the inner ones
nasty suggests the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A horrible accident casts a shadow over the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges 'crash' to ARCHS, and 'overshadowing' wraps it round ER. 17 4 is RADIO 4, the BBC station that broadcasts The Archers, a long-running rural soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archers are the farming family at the heart of the BBC radio soap opera.

clue.text: Time limit for film

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: A deadline for finishing a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Spellbound is Hitchcock's 1945 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound is the title of Alfred Hitchcock's 1945 psychological thriller.

clue.text: Immerse criminal character to end film

indicators.note: to end places this piece at the end of the answer
criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their lawful order

parts.note: zed is the British name of the letter Z, a character

explanation.surface: Plunging a crooked figure into the finale of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges 'Immerse' to MESMERI, and 'to end' puts the British name for the letter Z after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmerized is the title of a 1986 movie starring Jodie Foster.

clue.text: Bald athlete running in your old film

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the outer word

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hairless sprinter competes in an old movie of yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges 'Bald athlete' and 'in' puts the result inside THY. That'll Be the Day is a 1973 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: That'll Be the Day is the title of a 1973 British rock-and-roll movie.

clue.text: No villain ever guarding ship's chest

parts.note: the Bond villain No is Dr No, so the villain No has the title DR

indicators.note: guarding means the outer word surrounds and protects the inner one

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
SS, steamship, is the abbreviation before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A claim that no baddie ever protected a vessel's treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' looks like a negative but is the Bond villain Dr No. 'guarding' puts the ship abbreviation inside the poetic form of ever, making ESSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a chest of drawers, a piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Sellers wants lead in comedy instead of Western film

indicators.note: instead of signals one letter swapped in place of another within the word

parts.note: hawkers are street sellers

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers wants a starring role in a comedy rather than a cowboy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like the comic actor Peter Sellers but means street traders. 'instead of' swaps C, the first letter of 'comedy', for W in HAWKERS. Hackers is a 1995 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackers is the title of a 1995 movie about computer intruders.

clue.text: Unable to produce erotic film

parts.note: a shop that is out of the goods cannot supply them
blue means smutty or erotic, as in a blue movie

explanation.surface: Someone cannot make a pornographic movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'out of the' blue stuff means you cannot produce it. Out of the Blue is a 1980 Dennis Hopper movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of the Blue is the title of a 1980 movie directed by Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Author climbing tower, opening for film

parts.note: the author of a clue speaks of himself as me

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a silo is a tall tower for storing grain
a port is an opening, as in a porthole

explanation.surface: A writer scales a tower to get a start in movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SILO and PORT together, giving TROPOLIS. Metropolis is Fritz Lang's 1927 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Metropolis is the title of Fritz Lang's 1927 science-fiction silent movie.

clue.text: Notice collar held by member of wildlife film

indicators.note: held by means these letters sit inside the outer word

parts.note: a deer is one kind of wild animal
an ad is a notice or advertisement
a ring is a collar round the neck

explanation.surface: An advert for a collar worn by a creature in a nature documentary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts the notice and the collar inside the animal. Dead Ringer is a 1964 Bette Davis movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead Ringer is the title of a 1964 thriller starring Bette Davis.

clue.text: Basic wing nuts securing end of pole

indicators.note: securing means the outer letters hold the inner one fast

parts.note: an el (or ell) is a wing built at right angles to a main building
nuts and mental both mean crazy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Simple wing nuts are bolted round the tip of a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wing nuts' reads as hardware but is two separate pieces; 'securing' holds E, the last letter of 'pole', between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental describes something fundamental or rudimentary, which is what basic means.

clue.text: Type of screen from Japan, one attached to small house

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothes sizes
J is the international vehicle code for Japan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A screen from Japan is fixed to a small home.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoji is a translucent paper sliding partition used in Japanese houses.

clue.text: Extreme 'ego' gets Oscar for film

parts.note: rad, short for radical, means extreme
the ego is the self, I
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An over-the-top egotist wins an Oscar for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award but is the phonetic-alphabet word for O. Radio is a 2003 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is the title of a 2003 sports drama starring Cuba Gooding Jr.

clue.text: Bloke is waving dagger

indicators.note: waving suggests the letters flapping about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is brandishing a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dagger' looks like a weapon but is the printer's symbol, also called an obelisk or obelus.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing an obelisk is the dagger-shaped reference mark.

clue.text: Host almost welcomes new take on green issue

indicators.note: welcomes means the outer word takes the inner letters in
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: an emcee, MC, is the host of a show

indicators.note: a new take on a word rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A presenter nearly adopts a fresh approach to an environmental question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the final E from the host; 'new take on' rearranges 'green', and 'welcomes' puts that inside. 'issue' means something coming out, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergence is a coming out, and an issue is also something that comes out.

clue.text: Grumble about beginning and end of every film

indicators.note: about means the outer word wraps around the inner letters

parts.note: growl means grumble

indicators.note: the beginning and end of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Complaining about the opening and close of every movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning and end of' picks E and Y from 'every', and 'about' puts GROWL round them. Grey Owl is a 1999 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey Owl is the title of a 1999 biopic starring Pierce Brosnan.

clue.text: About to abandon ship after snoops mentioned film

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other
mentioned means a word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: to pry is to snoop, so snoops gives pries

indicators.note: to abandon means letters leave the word they were in

parts.note: a freighter is a cargo ship
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A sailor leaves a vessel once spies have been named in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snoops' looks like a noun but is the verb. 'to abandon' takes RE out of the cargo vessel, and 'after' puts that behind the sound of PRIES. The Prize Fighter is a 1979 movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prize Fighter is a 1979 boxing comedy movie.

clue.text: Short subject for film

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a theme is a subject

explanation.surface: A brief topic for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last E from THEME. Them! is a 1954 science-fiction movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Them! is the title of a 1954 science-fiction movie about giant ants.

clue.text: My heart is lifted, closer to Heaven — appropriate title for one?

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the letters read upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: the closer to a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: My spirit is raised nearer to heaven, a fitting name for a sacred song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lifted' turns MY and H together to HYM, and 'closer to' adds N from 'Heaven'. The clue's opening reads like a hymn's title, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as 'My heart is lifted, closer to Heaven' sound like the title of a sacred song of praise.

clue.text: Insulation failing, indication of temperature dropping

indicators.note: dropping means the letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: flagging means weakening or failing
F, Fahrenheit, shows a temperature scale

explanation.surface: Insulation is breaking down, as shown by the thermometer falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes F (Fahrenheit) from FLAGGING. Lagging is the wrapping put round pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging is the material wrapped round pipes and tanks to keep heat in.

clue.text: Good to keep mum in rainproofed carriage

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the outer word

parts.note: something rainproofed stays dry

indicators.note: to keep means the outer word holds the inner one

parts.note: OK means good or acceptable
mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A fine way to keep mother sheltered in a waterproof coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means quiet. 'to keep' puts the hush inside OK, and 'in' puts OSHK inside the rainproofed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A droshky is a low open horse-drawn carriage from Russia.

clue.text: Son's three-wheeler used in film

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a trike is a tricycle, with three wheels

explanation.surface: A boy's tricycle appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike (1925) is Eisenstein's silent movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Strike is the title of Sergei Eisenstein's 1925 silent movie.

clue.text: Well, well — actor makes film

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like well, well
Gary Oldman is an English actor

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as a performer directs a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, well' is an exclamation of surprise, MY. Gary Oldman is the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: My Old Man is the title of a British comedy movie.
